title: Modi at Somnath: Faith, Forex, and a Call for Austerity
excerpt: PM leads 75th-anniversary celebrations at the sacred Jyotirlinga shrine and urges Indians to cut gold imports amid global tensions.
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday led the Somnath Amrut Mahotsav in Gujarat's Gir Somnath district, performing sacred rituals at one of Hinduism's holiest shrines and using the occasion to deliver a pointed economic message to the nation.

**What happened at Somnath:**
Modi performed 'Maha Pooja' and other rituals at the Somnath Temple as part of the Amrut Mahotsav, marking 75 years of the inauguration of the restored shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva. He also released a commemorative postage stamp and a special Rs 75 coin during a public gathering, following participation in the Kumbhabhishek and Dhwaj Puja ceremonies. The celebrations featured an aerial display by the Indian Air Force's Suryakiran Aerobatic Team, cultural performances, and ceremonial rituals attended by thousands of devotees.

**The economic appeal:**
Modi appealed to citizens to defer gold buying in view of the prevailing global situation, noting that a significant amount of foreign exchange goes into importing the precious metal. He stressed the need for reduced imports — India heavily relies on West Asia for crude oil and LPG — and urged avoiding unnecessary expenditure involving foreign currency. Calling for fuel conservation, he urged people to reduce fuel consumption and shift to public transport or electric vehicles.

**The civilisational message:**
Modi declared that India's 1951 Pran Pratishtha at Somnath was a proclamation of India's 'awakened and free consciousness,' and that Sardar Patel's reconstruction sent a message that India had embarked on reclaiming its ancient civilisation. The Prime Minister said the Somnath Amrut Mahotsav will not merely remain a celebration of the past, but will continue to serve as a source of inspiration for India over the next thousand years.

**What to watch:**
Titan, Kalyan Jewellers, and other gold-linked stocks plunged up to 12 per cent following the Prime Minister's appeal — markets and policymakers will track whether Modi's call translates into a sustained government-level curb on gold imports.
